heading: Delhi election results | Highlight: Arvind Kejriwal meets newly elected AAP MLAs
paragraphs:
Delhi election results | Highlights: In a historic victory, the Bharatiya Janata Party has come to power in the national capital after 27 years, securing 48 out of 70 seats in the Delhi assembly elections, according to the Election Commission of India. The incumbent Aam Admi Party managed to secure 22 seats but fell short of the majority.

BJP leader Parvesh Verma defeated AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal in a high-stakes battle. AAP leader and Delhi chief minister Atishi, however, managed to win the Kalkaji seat against BJP's Ramesh Bidhuri. She resigned from her position as chief minister on Sunday.

Lt Governor V K Saxena has also issued an order to dissolve the legislative assembly effective immediately. BJP's winning candidates Parvesh Verma and Kailash Gahlot also visited the Raj Niwas to meet the Lt Governor.

BJP supporters have been celebrating the result in the city, with prime minister Narendra Modi giving an address at the BJP headquarters to congratulate party workers.

The election results can be checked on https://results.eci.gov.in

-Election Commission of India (ECI) declares results: According to final data from the Election Commission, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has officially won 48 seats. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), meanwhile, has won 22 seats as per the final EC tally.

-Delhi election results | Counting time: The counting of votes for Delhi assembly election 2025 began at 8 am on February 8, 2025. Voting for Delhi assembly poll 2025 took place in a single phase on February 5.

-Delhi voter turnout: According to EC figures, the approximate voter turnout after the Delhi assembly election stood at 60.54 per cent.

-Delhi election | Key parties: The incumbent AAP, BJP and the Congress were the main contenders of Delhi poll 2025. AAP was eyeing a third straight full term in Delhi. AAP, which has dominated the last two assembly polls in Delhi, won 62 out of 70 seats in the 2020 election, while the BJP won eight.

-Delhi election results | Congress fails to open account: Congress, which ruled Delhi for 15 years, failed to open its account in the last two assembly polls and has performed similarly this time as well, scoring zero.

-Delhi election results 2025 | Key winners: BJP's Parvesh Verma was the top nam among key winners of the Delhi assembly election, defeating AAP supremo and former Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal. While most top guns of AAP failed to fire, party's Atishi won the Kalkaji seat against BJP's Ramesh Bidhuri. AAP leader Gopal Rai also won the Babarpur seat.

-Delhi election results 2025 | Key losers: AAP's Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia and Saurabh Bharadwaj are among the top losers of Delhi assembly election. BJP's Ramesh Bidhuri has also lost from Kalkaji against AAP leader and CM Atishi.

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Sunday said that the Chief Minister face in Delhi will be decided by the top leadership of the party, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and party's national president JP Nadda.
AAP's actions during the past 10 years in Delhi led to its decline, former IPS officer Kiran Bedi said on Sunday.
"It (AAP) lost because of its own actions. I am speaking as a citizen about the decline I witnessed in the last 10 years," she told PTI Videos.
Newly elected BJP MLA from New Delhi, Parvesh Verma, on Sunday, quoted Pakistani poet Habib Jalib to take a dig at AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal. READ FULL STORY

BJP's winning candidate from Matiala assembly Sandeep Sehrawat on Sunday said, “I come from a simple family and PM Modi has given his blessings. We will fulfil the responsibility we have been given and as a worker, we will complete our work.”
Union minister Piyush Goyal on Sunday said the Delhi assembly poll results would be remembered as a turning point for the people who unmasked AAP and its supremo Arvind Kejriwal.
Speaking to reporters in Gondia in Maharashtra, Goyal alleged that the Aam Aadmi Party deprived Delhi of development and promoted corruption.
AAP's Okhla MLA Amanatullah Khan on Sunday blamed the Congress for the party's defeat in the Delhi polls, a charge rubbished by the grand old party.

"The Congress contested the election not to win but to ensure our defeat. Rahul Gandhi came to campaign in my constituency for the first time ever. It knew it had no chance of winning but was determined to make us lose," Khan said.
AAP leader alleged that both parties had contested the elections not to win but to defeat AAP and "Congress put all its strength to defeat AAP."

“BJP has benefitted from Congress. Congress and AIMIM did not fight to win, they only wanted to defeat AAP. They have a very crucial role in the defeat of AAP and Congress put all its strength to defeat AAP,” Khan stated on Sunday while speaking to ANI.

BJP's winning candidate from the R K Puram Assembly constituency, Anil Sharma on Sunday said "The people of Delhi wanted development and they have voted for that development. We will fulfil all the guarantees made to the people of Delhi.
Outgoing Delhi chief minister Atishi accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of indulging in “hooliganism” to secure victory in the recently concluded assembly election. READ FULL STORY
AAP leader Manish Sisodia on Sunday said that Arvind Kejriwal boosted the morale of the AAP MLAs and asked them to serve the people of their respective constituencies.

“Arvind Kejriwal boosted the morale of those AAP candidates who were not able to win the elections. Everyone fought the elections very well, while the entire machinery was used, money, and liquor were distributed openly. The rules of the Election Commission of India and the Model Code of Conduct were violated. We will serve the people in our respective constituencies,” Sisodia said.

A day after the AAP was ousted from power in Delhi, party supremo Arvind Kejriwal on Sunday met its 22 newly elected MLAs at his Ferozshah Road residence in Delhi and asked them to work for the people.

Outgoing Delhi chief minister Atishi, whose party suffered a huge setback in the recently concluded Delhi assembly election, said that her party will work as a constructive opposition and will ensure that the BJP gives ₹2,500 to women, free power and continues other facilities for Delhi people.

Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini said the people of Delhi endorsed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's guarantees, and asserted that the national capital would now stride firmly towards a "Viksit Bharat".

The BJP's vote share in Delhi has grown by nearly 13 percentage points in the last 10 years while the AAP's vote share has declined by nearly 10 percentage points during the same period, reported PTI.

BJP leader Tarvinder Singh Marwah, who defeated AAP heavyweight Manish Sisodia from Delhi's Jangpura assembly constituency, alleged that the former deputy chief minister's campaign was focussed on labelling him a ‘goonda’ in every public meeting. READ FULL STORY

Following the Bhartiya Janata Party's historic victory in the Delhi Assembly elections, the party's winning candidate from Shalimar Bagh, Rekha Gupta called the near-decade rule of Aam Aadmi Party in the national capital as a "AAPda" for Delhi.

JP's Punjab General Secretary, Anil Sarin on Sunday criticised the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and accused it of making false promises He further predicted that AAP would be ousted from power in Punjab as well, asserting that "lies and fraud cannot last long."
Rajya Sabha MP Swati Maliwal on Sunday took a dig at Aam Aadmi Party leader Atishi after she was seen celebrating her victory from the Kalkaji constituency in the assembly elections.

"Atishi should be ashamed. Her party has suffered a huge defeat. All their main leaders have lost. Yet, she did a roadshow to celebrate her win and even danced during it. What is she celebrating? Her party's loss?" Maliwal said
Hailing BJP's performance in the recently concluded assembly elections, BJP leader Gourav Vallabh on Sunday said that the people of Delhi have defeated the perpetrators of corruption.

“The people of Delhi have awarded defeat to all the perpetrators of corruption in Delhi. Congress is no longer a party, they are just passing time. What can one say about those who consider themselves heroes even after getting zero votes three times? AAP has now become history. It has no future,” said Vallabh.
RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday said that the BJP's victory in the Delhi assembly polls will not have any impact in Bihar where elections are due later this year.
The former deputy chief minister of Bihar also said that a return to power "after nearly 26 years" made it incumbent upon the BJP to fulfil the promises made to the people of Delhi.

Delhi election final result LIVE: BJP leader Parvesh Verma, who defeated Arvind Kejriwal to secure the New Delhi assembly seat, was seen distributing sweets among people in celebration of BJP's historic victory.
Delhi election final result LIVE: Union minister G Kishan Reddy and BJP MP K Laxman celebrated the Delhi election win with supporters in Hyderabad.

Delhi election final result LIVE: Amid celebrations in support of the BJPs' historic electoral win in Delhi, BJP MP Dr K Laxman told ANI, "The people are excited for the BJP to also uproot the corrupt Congress government in Telangana. The lotus will bloom soon in Telangana."
Delhi election final result LIVE: BJP's winning candidate from Mustafabad seat, Mohan Singh Bisht said on Sunday that he would change the name of the constituency once he takes office.
"I had said that if I win I'll change the name of Mustafabad to Shiv Puri or Shiv Vihar. I'll do it," he said, as quoted by ANI.
